written.myAnswer: Atmospheric pressure is balanced by the pressure of the mercury column: p_atm = ρgh. Thus, atmospheric pressure is measured from the height of the column.
Trapped air above the mercury exerts pressure and supports some of the column, so its height is less than it should be.
Air entering through the leak exerts pressure above the mercury, lowering the column and causing an incorrect barometer reading.

Air has weight and exerts pressure in all directions on objects and surfaces. Atmospheric pressure is used in a drinking straw, a syringe or dropper, and a suction pump; a barometer measures it, and its changes can help forecast weather.
The water column would be about 10.3 m high.
